newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends steady after dull session.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends steady after dull session.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed steady after another listless session due to lack of consumer demand, traders said.
They said the steadiness reflected a continued technical adjustment after earlier falls.
"There's some adjustment of prices but there's still no buyers in the market," said one trader.

She said the market's upside appears limited given the continuing absence of buyers. "Producers still have a lot of stocks to clear and they may be forced to sell even at cheaper levels," the trader said.
At the close, benchmark March RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 304.50 cents ($1.22) a kg, up a cent from Tuesday.
March SMR 20 buyer closed unchanged at 299 cents ($1.20).
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 299 cents a kg, SMR CV at 360, SMR L at 340, SMR 5 at 308, SMR 10 at 300 and drum latex FOB at 239.
The INRO five-day moving average was 234.97 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Feb 18 against 234.60 on Feb 17. The daily indicator price was 235.27 versus 234.10.
